name: Malaysian Mahjong
description: Malaysian Mahjong is a Southeast Asian Mahjong profile with expanded bonus and joker-style tiles in many common sets. It uses a larger 160-tile composition and local scoring conventions.

overview.description: Malaysian Mahjong is a Southeast Asian Mahjong profile with expanded bonus and joker-style tiles in many common sets. It uses a larger 160-tile composition and local scoring conventions.

history.origins: Malaysian Mahjong developed as a regional profile using expanded tile sets and local scoring conventions.
timeline: Modern era: expanded 160-tile sets become common in local play.
history.cultural: It is played widely in social and club contexts in Malaysia and nearby regions.
history.evolution: Expanded tile families and local bonus handling distinguish Malaysian table profiles.

setup.deck: 160-tile Mahjong set with expanded bonus/joker-style groups.
setup.dealing: Each player receives 13 tiles; dealer receives 14 and discards first.

rules.objective: Complete a legal winning hand and satisfy active Malaysian scoring rules.
rules.gameplay: Players draw and discard in turn, claim legal sets by priority, and resolve expanded bonus/joker-style tiles according to profile conventions.
keyRules: Draw then discard is the core loop.
Claim legality and priority determine interruptions.
Expanded bonus and joker-style tile handling follows local profile rules.

strategy.basic: Build efficient waits while maintaining defensive discard discipline.
strategy.intermediate: Track visible bonus/joker exposure and opponent tempo for safer discards.
strategy.advanced: Optimize speed versus value while accounting for expanded tile interactions and local scoring pressure.
tips: Do not overcommit to fragile value lines.
Use defensive timing when opponents show coherent completion routes.
